name: Lieutenant Kirtar
title: The Order's Lieutenant
role: Order officer and early possessor of the Mirari
summary: An Order commander who took the Mirari from the Cabal but could not make its power serve his ideal of justice.
biography: Kirtar served the Order, which opposed the Cabal and claimed to act against the dangerous magic and cruelty associated with Cabal City.

When the Mirari passed from Cabal custody into the Order's hands, Kirtar hoped to direct its power toward his cause. The artifact instead demonstrated how dangerous certainty could become when amplified by overwhelming magic.
His failure is one phase of the Mirari's passage among rival Otarian powers, preceding Aboshan's disastrous use of the sphere.

Kirtar was an officer in an organization that defined itself in opposition to the Cabal. Where Cabal arenas made suffering into a marketable spectacle, the Order claimed a higher authority rooted in discipline and justice. That contrast made the Mirari attractive as a way to secure the Order's position.

The sphere's effect was more complicated than an ordinary weapon changing hands. Kirtar believed the legitimacy of his ends would help control what he possessed, but the Mirari exposed the gap between moral conviction and restraint. His attempt belongs beside later failures by rulers and warriors who brought different ambitions to the same object.

His portrait is evidence of his presence in the Odyssey story, not a literal depiction of the Mirari's decisive transformation of him. Preserving that distinction keeps the illustrated archive from confusing character identification with an exact historical event scene.

featuredCard.significance: Kirtar's original Odyssey portrait; the illustration identifies him rather than depicting his final attempt to wield the Mirari.
